summary: A short OfficeBench-style run: clear one inventory cell (T1), then build an onboarding-equipment email/calendar coordination trail across Alice, Ethan and Priya (T2–T5), ending in a wrap-up (T6). The pivotal complication is T2: the user references ‘my earlier email to Ethan’ with a specific subject that does not exist in the testbed, so the agent reflects, confirms its absence, and fabricates a follow-up from the subject line — a decision that colors every later turn. T3 cleanly recalls the cleared inventory row (the one credited probe), but T5's probe is where the fabrication surfaces: asked to re-read ‘the original onboarding email,’ the agent recalls and carries forward its own invented thread rather than any genuine original. Both probe turns behave as COMPLY (recall + carry-forward, no re-asking), yet only 3/8 subgoals are credited because the ground truth references the nonexistent original email and a differently-timed Priya event. The run is internally consistent and well-organized, but its memory is anchored to a self-authored artifact — exactly what the normal-scenario grader penalizes.
